name: application-permission-denied
title: Permission Denied State
description: Locked panel explaining why access was denied, with a request-access action that transitions into a confirmed pending state.
useWhen: A user navigates to a resource they lack the role or permission to view.
You want to explain the specific reason for denial (missing role, team membership) rather than a generic 403.
Self-service access requests are supported and the user can trigger one directly from this state.
avoidWhen: The user isn't authenticated at all — redirect to a sign-in flow instead of showing a permission-denied panel.
There's simply no data yet (not a permission issue) — use empty-states instead, which doesn't imply the user did anything wrong.
Access requests aren't self-service in your product — drop the CTA and link to documentation or support instead.
responsiveBehavior: The panel is a fixed max-w-sm card that centers itself in its container at all viewport widths.
accessibility: The initial denied state uses role="alert" so screen readers announce it as soon as it renders.
The pending state after requesting access uses role="status" (not alert) since it's a confirmation, not an urgent interruption.
The disabled 'Request sent' button uses the native disabled attribute so it's correctly excluded from the tab order.

variants.title: Permission denied
variants.description: Locked-icon panel with a specific denial reason and a Request access button.
accessibility: role="alert" ensures the denial is announced without requiring the user to find and focus the panel.

variants.title: Permission denied (Dark)
variants.description: Permission denied panel adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Icon, heading, and button colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.

variants.title: Request sent
variants.description: Confirmation state after the user requests access: checkmark icon, confirmation copy, and a disabled 'Request sent' button.
accessibility: role="status" announces the confirmation politely rather than interrupting like an alert.

variants.title: Request sent (Dark)
variants.description: Request-sent confirmation state adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Success icon and disabled-button colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
